title: Building the air combat simulator I always wanted: Vector Flight
author: L0rdCha0s
selftext:
Focus on realism and accuracy (please point out anything you see that doesn't look / act right).

As you can see, focusing on the F-35B/C for now.  I have sourced as much on the behaviour of the cockpit screens as possible, which has been very hard to locate.

The nuclear explosions (ground/air land/sea bursts) are still a work in progress but coming along nicely.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/L0rdCha0s please expand this post with how you used AI during development. It's not enough to say you used AI. Tell us what you did with it. The point of Rule 4 is for promotional posts to give something back by sharing the process and actual development. We're cracking down on posts that only advertise. If you don't update, this may be removed.

comments.author: wwlima
comments.body: Loved the g force effect with low or high blood pressure in the head of the pilot! I will actually use this ideia in my game too! lol

replies.author: L0rdCha0s
replies.body: I can't take credit - I borrowed it in turn from Lock On: Modern Air Combat, circa 2003!

comments.author: SomnambulisticTaco
comments.body: Show it photos and video of real shockwaves in water and have it use those as references EVERY iteration

replies.author: L0rdCha0s
replies.body:
yep - actually working on this right now - i have a series of videos of real airbursts / ground bursts above land and water.    
  
Trying to allocate my tokens sensibly - the current nuke effects took around 10% of weekly usage on 6.2-extra high, so iterating between different things.

replies.author: SomnambulisticTaco
replies.body:
Understood.  
Make sure they look at them every single turn. A picture is worth a thousand words

replies.author: L0rdCha0s
replies.body: I've actually been amazed at how well it cycles on this kind of thing - I did the same for hours with cockpit visuals and controls, and various other components... chasing perfection seems to be a hobby for the model..
